abstract: Maintains surface leveling benchmarks and satellite radar interferometry networks
system_message:
You are Geodetic survey supervisor (GEOD). The Geodetic survey supervisor (GEOD) oversees geodetic monitoring operations, maintaining surface leveling benchmarks and satellite radar interferometry networks across prospective subterranean energy storage facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Borehole tiltmeter calibration（TILT）
information_points.content:
GEOD-TILT-S89：Calibration records for the Salina Basin Bedded Halite Formation indicate a borehole tilt drift of 18 microradians, representing the maximum ninety-day angular drift of the primary tilt axis for the subsurface tiltmeter installed at the cavern casing shoe.
GEOD-TILT-3CV：According to the borehole sensor calibration sheet for the Prairie Evaporite Cavern Complex, the borehole tilt drift is 12 microradians, reflecting the maximum ninety-day angular drift of the primary tilt axis recorded at the cavern casing shoe.
GEOD-TILT-SR8：For the Paradox Valley Salt Dome Testbed, borehole tiltmeter calibration records show a borehole tilt drift of 5 microradians, measured as the maximum ninety-day angular drift of the primary tilt axis at the cavern casing shoe.

information_points.title: Maintains surface leveling benchmarks and satellite radar interferometry networks（SURF）
information_points.content:
GEOD-SURF-Y1Y：For the Prairie Evaporite Cavern Complex, baseline geodetic subsidence array readiness is confirmed as true following the formal commissioning of fixed GNSS monuments and the baseline differential level loop across the two-kilometer radial surface network around the candidate wellhead.
GEOD-SURF-7M3：For the Paradox Valley Salt Dome Testbed, baseline geodetic subsidence array readiness is false, as formal commissioning of fixed GNSS monuments and the baseline differential level loop across the two-kilometer radial surface network around the candidate wellhead has not been attained.
GEOD-SURF-UM0：For the Salina Basin Bedded Halite Formation, baseline geodetic subsidence array readiness is confirmed as true based on the formal commissioning of fixed GNSS monuments and baseline differential level loops across the two-kilometer radial surface network around the candidate wellhead.
